answer: To deter Sybil attacks, the network routes verification through a spectral stake-slashing mechanism: each agent projects its identity through a cryptographic prism that splits identity claims across a multidimensional stake ridge. Registering n identities requires quadratic stake burning scaled by S(n) = k · n^2, imposing superlinear attacker cost. Honest agents freely coordinate across the consensus meadow, while adversaries face prohibitive capital depletion.
